# DRISTI 2.0 - Domain Model

> A data-driven reference of the legal domain a court **case type** is built on. Two case types are modelled: **Cheque bounce** (NI Act, 1881 · §138) and **Transfer dishonour** (PSS Act, 2007 · §25). Each has its own bundle, digest and profile, listed below. The site is a static viewer that reads the corpus at runtime; every data file is fetchable directly.

For agents: start with the denormalized bundle for the case type you are working on - it joins that case type's profile with the Akoma Ntoso statute text, and with the state layers, the field notes and the normative requirements where that case type has them, into one document, each node carrying a shareable deep link (a `#...` URL fragment). Then use the schemas and data dictionary to read the raw files directly. Counts differ by case type and so does coverage: where a case type does not model a layer, its profile says so in `scope` and the bundle carries the reason instead of an empty list.

## The case types (start here - one bundle each)

Field meanings and enumerations for all of them are in [/domain/data-dictionary.md](/domain/data-dictionary.md), which also tabulates what each case type does and does not model.

### Cheque bounce - NI Act, 1881 · §138

> Dishonour of a cheque for insufficiency of funds - a criminal complaint. Around 15% of a typical court's caseload; high volume, relatively standard.

- [/domain/cheque-dishonour-s138.json](/domain/cheque-dishonour-s138.json): the full domain bundle as JSON - 108 provisions across 21 Acts, 91 national terms, 42 edges between them, 43 judgments, 493 normative requirements, 3 state layers.
- [/domain/cheque-dishonour-s138.md](/domain/cheque-dishonour-s138.md): the same as a readable digest.
- [/data/profiles/cheque-dishonour-s138.profile.json](/data/profiles/cheque-dishonour-s138.profile.json): the raw relevance profile - the Acts it draws on, the provisions pinned inside them, and the vocabulary.
- [/data/caselaw/cheque-dishonour-s138.caselaw.json](/data/caselaw/cheque-dishonour-s138.caselaw.json): the case-law dataset, 43 judgments.

### Transfer dishonour - PSS Act, 2007 · §25

> Dishonour of an electronic funds transfer for insufficiency of funds - the sibling offence to a cheque bounce, drafted as a deliberate parallel of it and then, in s.25(5), told to borrow the cheque machinery 'to the extent the circumstances admit'. Low volume and almost no reported authority; a first cut that names its own gaps.

- [/domain/eft-dishonour-s25.json](/domain/eft-dishonour-s25.json): the full domain bundle as JSON - 96 provisions across 18 Acts, 64 national terms, 67 edges between them.
- [/domain/eft-dishonour-s25.md](/domain/eft-dishonour-s25.md): the same as a readable digest.
- [/data/profiles/eft-dishonour-s25.profile.json](/data/profiles/eft-dishonour-s25.profile.json): the raw relevance profile - the Acts it draws on, the provisions pinned inside them, and the vocabulary.

Not modelled for this case type, in the profile's own words - these are findings about the law and the corpus, not gaps left silent:

- **State layers.** This is a first cut. It models the shared central core only. There is no state layer for this case type: no High Court rules, no e-filing rules, no court-fee entry, no special-court notification, no local practice. Where the s.138 profile has Kerala, Gujarat and Haryana overlays, this one has nothing, and the state pages will show the not-modelled placeholder.

- **Case law.** No case-law dataset is linked, and that is a finding rather than an omission of effort. Section 25 has been on the statute book since 2008 and there is, so far as this pass could establish, effectively no reported Supreme Court authority construing it - no analogue of Rangappa on the presumption, of Dashrath Rupsingh on where the complaint lies, of Damodar S. Prabhu on compounding. The case type is therefore modelled almost entirely from the text of the Acts. The practical consequence is that the open questions recorded in the notes below - the limitation period, the place of trial, which compounding power governs - have no judicial answer to cite, only an argument either way.

- **Normative requirements.** The normative layer (what a system MUST do to run one of these cases lawfully) is not derived for this case type. The 493 requirements in this corpus are all written against s.138 and none of them has been re-tested against s.25.

- **State vocabulary.** The terms below are the national vocabulary only. There is no state vocabulary layer.

## The normative layer - what a system MUST do (493 requirements)

The rest of the corpus is descriptive: it says what the law provides, and a description validates nothing. These are statements that BIND a system - each derived from a named provision, each with a `test` you can run against a screen, a schema or a workflow. If you are building or auditing a system for **Cheque bounce**, start here. They are written against that case type and have not been re-derived for any other; `eft-dishonour-s25` says so in its `scope`.

- [/data/requirements/national.json](/data/requirements/national.json): 172 requirements derived from central law and Supreme Court case law. **Binds every state.**
- [/data/requirements/gujarat.json](/data/requirements/gujarat.json): 127 requirements added by Gujarat's own instruments, or where one of them tightens a national requirement.
- [/data/requirements/haryana.json](/data/requirements/haryana.json): 84 requirements added by Haryana's own instruments, or where one of them tightens a national requirement.
- [/data/requirements/kerala.json](/data/requirements/kerala.json): 110 requirements added by Kerala's own instruments, or where one of them tightens a national requirement.
- [/data/requirements/README.md](/data/requirements/README.md): the spec - every field, the category codes, the id grammar.
- [/data/schema/requirement.schema.json](/data/schema/requirement.schema.json): the schema.
- All of them, with each `authority` cite resolved to its section number and heading, are in the `cheque-dishonour-s138` bundle under `requirements`, and in its digest under "Normative requirements".

## Raw data (source of truth)
- Relevance profiles, one per case type: [/data/profiles/cheque-dishonour-s138.profile.json](/data/profiles/cheque-dishonour-s138.profile.json) · [/data/profiles/eft-dishonour-s25.profile.json](/data/profiles/eft-dishonour-s25.profile.json)
- [/data/config/app.config.json](/data/config/app.config.json): case types (each naming its profile), jurisdictions, field notes.
- State layers: [/data/state/gujarat.json](/data/state/gujarat.json) · [/data/state/haryana.json](/data/state/haryana.json) · [/data/state/kerala.json](/data/state/kerala.json) - written against **Cheque bounce**; a case type with no state layer says so in its profile `scope`.
- Case law: [/data/caselaw/cheque-dishonour-s138.caselaw.json](/data/caselaw/cheque-dishonour-s138.caselaw.json)
- Statute corpus: 24 Akoma Ntoso XML files under [/data/acts/akn/](/data/acts/akn/) (national) and /data/state/<state>/akn/, shared by every case type that pins them.

## Standards adherence (the non-legal layer, 41 standards)

The requirements above are what the *law* compels. These are what any public digital service owes the person using it, which a court-facing one owes more heavily: accessibility, security, performance, interoperability, usability and content. Markdown rather than JSON because the content is prose; every entry carries a test and the threshold that decides it. This layer and the two below it - policy, model rules - are corpus-wide: they are not written per case type and they bind a build whichever case type it serves.

- [/data/standards/standards-adherence.md](/data/standards/standards-adherence.md): 41 standards across Accessibility, Security, Performance, Interoperability, Usability, Content & Legal. The file states its own shape in a comment at the top.

## Policy (8 documents) and policy compliance (86 records)

A policy is the third kind of instrument here. Akoma Ntoso has no policy document type, so each one is carried as `<doc name="...">` - the element the standard provides for a document type it does not name - with @name saying which kind it is (policy, procedure, regulations, rules), and it would be `<act>` once notified into force. The checked transcription sits in policy/md/ and the source PDF one folder over; `policy.json` is the manifest, and it also declares how each document numbers itself, which is the stem its clause eIds use: regulation 43(3) is `reg_43_3`, rule 10.3 is `rule_10_3`. The compliance file pulls out every operational obligation - anything that must be reported, disclosed, logged, registered, audited, or produced as a record - and cites the clause it comes from. Each record separates what the document requires from what DRISTI suggests building; do not read the second as the first.

- [/data/policy/policy.json](/data/policy/policy.json): the manifest - each document's issuer, status, unit of numbering, markdown, source PDF and source URL.
- [/data/policy/akn/regulations-for-use-of-artificial-intelligence-in-courts-2026.akn.xml](/data/policy/akn/regulations-for-use-of-artificial-intelligence-in-courts-2026.akn.xml): Regulations for Use of Artificial Intelligence in Courts, 2026 (Supreme Court of India, draft). Transcription: [/data/policy/md/regulations-for-use-of-artificial-intelligence-in-courts-2026.md](/data/policy/md/regulations-for-use-of-artificial-intelligence-in-courts-2026.md).
- [/data/policy/akn/model-rules-for-e-filing-2020.akn.xml](/data/policy/akn/model-rules-for-e-filing-2020.akn.xml): Model Rules for e-Filing (Rules for On-line Electronic Filing framed under Articles 225 and 227 of the Constitution of India) (e-Committee, Supreme Court of India, model). Transcription: [/data/policy/md/model-rules-for-e-filing-2020.md](/data/policy/md/model-rules-for-e-filing-2020.md).
- [/data/policy/akn/model-rules-for-video-conferencing-for-courts-2020.akn.xml](/data/policy/akn/model-rules-for-video-conferencing-for-courts-2020.akn.xml): Model Rules for Video Conferencing for Courts (e-Committee, Supreme Court of India, model). Transcription: [/data/policy/md/model-rules-for-video-conferencing-for-courts-2020.md](/data/policy/md/model-rules-for-video-conferencing-for-courts-2020.md).
- [/data/policy/akn/model-rules-for-live-streaming-and-recording-2022.akn.xml](/data/policy/akn/model-rules-for-live-streaming-and-recording-2022.akn.xml): Model Rules for Live Streaming and Recording of Court Proceedings (e-Committee, Supreme Court of India, model). Transcription: [/data/policy/md/model-rules-for-live-streaming-and-recording-2022.md](/data/policy/md/model-rules-for-live-streaming-and-recording-2022.md).
- [/data/policy/akn/sop-for-preparing-accessible-court-documents-2022.akn.xml](/data/policy/akn/sop-for-preparing-accessible-court-documents-2022.akn.xml): Standard Operating Procedure for Preparing Accessible Court Documents (e-Committee, Supreme Court of India, model). Transcription: [/data/policy/md/sop-for-preparing-accessible-court-documents-2022.md](/data/policy/md/sop-for-preparing-accessible-court-documents-2022.md).
- [/data/policy/akn/policy-action-plan-phase-i-ecourts-2005.akn.xml](/data/policy/akn/policy-action-plan-phase-i-ecourts-2005.akn.xml): National Policy and Action Plan for Implementation of Information and Communication Technology in the Indian Judiciary (e-Committee, Supreme Court of India, superseded). Transcription: [/data/policy/md/policy-action-plan-phase-i-ecourts-2005.md](/data/policy/md/policy-action-plan-phase-i-ecourts-2005.md).
- [/data/policy/akn/policy-action-plan-phase-ii-ecourts-2014.akn.xml](/data/policy/akn/policy-action-plan-phase-ii-ecourts-2014.akn.xml): Policy and Action Plan Document, Phase II of the eCourts Project (Supreme Court of India, superseded). Transcription: [/data/policy/md/policy-action-plan-phase-ii-ecourts-2014.md](/data/policy/md/policy-action-plan-phase-ii-ecourts-2014.md).
- [/data/policy/akn/vision-document-phase-iii-ecourts-2022.akn.xml](/data/policy/akn/vision-document-phase-iii-ecourts-2022.akn.xml): Digital Courts: Vision & Roadmap - e-Courts Project Phase III (e-Committee, Supreme Court of India, current). Transcription: [/data/policy/md/vision-document-phase-iii-ecourts-2022.md](/data/policy/md/vision-document-phase-iii-ecourts-2022.md).
- [/data/standards/ai-policy-compliance.md](/data/standards/ai-policy-compliance.md): 86 compliance records (20 bind both, 65 bind court, 1 bind vendor), grouped by the document each one resolves against. Read as a sub-tab of Standards adherence in the viewer.

## Model rules (35 sections across 2 tabs)

The source is `Rules of Practice | Draft_Public Inputs` (Draft, out for public inputs). Kept as markdown rather than Akoma Ntoso on purpose: it is a draft, not an instrument in force anywhere, and <act> would assert a status it does not have. It reads under Design in the viewer, beside the standards, because it is something a build can be measured against rather than something the corpus holds as law. Each tab of the source document is one file and one sub-tab; the numbering in the files is the draft's own and is never regenerated.

- [/data/modelrules/modelrules.json](/data/modelrules/modelrules.json): the manifest - the tabs in reading order, and the source document behind them.
- [/data/modelrules/draft-rules.md](/data/modelrules/draft-rules.md): Draft Rules (33 sections).
- [/data/modelrules/objects-and-reasons.md](/data/modelrules/objects-and-reasons.md): Objects & Reasons (2 sections).

## Deep links
Append a fragment to the site root, e.g. `/#law?act=ni&eid=sec_138`, `/#story?state=haryana&sec=role-filing-assistant`, `/#words?state=kerala&term=scrutiny%20officer`, `/#practice?state=haryana&note=hr-filing-assistant-2026-06`.
